readers.reasoning: The worksharing-loop SIMD construct is orphaned inside the target region; it binds to the implicit parallel region, which is permitted. The array pointer o1 is not a scalar, so it is implicitly mapped tofrom, and an associated pointer in a map clause has its target implicitly mapped, so o1t is on the device. The loop writes distinct elements, so there is no race. Nothing in the program breaks a rule, so a conforming compiler must compile it; an internal compiler error is a compiler bug.

The do simd construct inside target has no enclosing parallel construct, so it binds to the implicit parallel region (one thread); that is a legal orphaned worksharing loop. o1 is a non-scalar Fortran pointer, so it is implicitly mapped tofrom, and its target is mapped with it. The j loop is a valid simd loop with no dependences (distinct o1(i,j) per iteration). A compiler ICE on a conforming program is an error.
